data.description:
## Problem

When the proxy returns a 503 'All providers exhausted' response, retry_after is **hardcoded to 60 seconds**. The Worklog extension's retry loop then waits 2 seconds, retries, fails again, and loops for up to ~60 seconds with exponential backoff — all while real provider availability is **minutes to hours away** (big-pickle cooldown: 86400s; go-2 reset: Aug 30; deepseek: outside available_times).

This wastes time and produces repeated error notifications that confuse the user.

## Solution

The proxy already collects per-provider availability data in unavailable_providers (cooldown maps) and knows about available_times windows. Compute the **real next-available time** and emit it as:

1. **A Retry-After HTTP header** (standard mechanism, integer seconds until retry is valid)
2. **The retry_after field** in the JSON response (already exists but is wrong)

### Implementation details

The proxy response is built in proxy/proxy/provider.py -> _build_exhausted_response() (or wherever the 503 is constructed). Compute the real retry_after as:

  retry_after = max(
      max(unavailable_providers.values()) if unavailable_providers else 0,
      next_available_times_window_edge(),
      next_usage_limit_reset()
  )

### Acceptance Criteria

1. retry_after in the JSON 503 response reflects the **real** next provider availability (not hardcoded 60).
2. A Retry-After HTTP header is set on 503 responses with the same value.
3. The value is the maximum of: cooldown durations, available_times window edges, and usage-limit reset times.
4. If all providers are actually available (edge case), retry_after = 0.
5. Existing tests pass (update any that assert retry_after == 60).
6. Full test suite passes (quiet mode).

### Related work

This is the **proxy-side** half of the fix. The **extension-side** half (Worklog ContextHub) is tracked separately: the Worklog recovery module's classifyError must recognize 'All providers exhausted' and route it to the retry loop with this new Retry-After delay.
data.title: Honest Retry-After: emit real provider availability windows

# Post-rollout proxy monitoring: warm/cold prefill ratio, fallback rate, remote spend, TTFT

Discovered from: LP-0MTAQNAIO0069DUP (ctx-config evaluation, commit a866aa1 to dev)

## Problem statement

After the persistence-cap rollout (LP-0MTBTCB8D000OQ0C) raises
`session_slot_max_prompt_tokens` to the routing clamp, the proxy's prefill/warm
behavior and fallback economics should shift measurably. This item instruments
and reports the change against the 2026-08-26 baseline captured in the
evaluation (42.7M prefill tokens/day, 4,541 fallbacks/day, `/v1/status` p50
1.9s, 280 backend 503s in hour 22).

## Scope

- Collect 48h of post-rollout metrics and compare against the 2026-08-26
  baseline (proxy-usage-reports data + /var/log/llama-proxy logs).
- Metrics: cold vs warm prefill ratio (warm = cache restore success), fallback
  rate per reason (context_too_large, local_concurrency_limit, local_lease_active,
  large_context_bypass), remote spend (remote requests per session), TTFT
  distribution, `available_slots=0` frequency, prefill tokens/day.
- Produce a before/after comparison table and a verdict: did the cap raise
  achieve the projected 61.9%→89.1% full-local share and reduce prefill volume?
- Record results as a comment on LP-0MTBTCB8D000OQ0C and this item.

## OUT OF SCOPE

- Any config/code change in this item (monitoring only)
- Changing the cap further (follow-up only if verdict says insufficient)

## Acceptance criteria

1. 48h post-rollout window defined with exact start/end timestamps; baseline
   window (2026-08-26) metrics restated.
2. Comparison table: prefill tokens/day, warm/cold ratio, fallback rate per
   reason, remote spend, TTFT p50/p95, available_slots=0 count — post vs
   baseline.
3. Verdict comment: cap-raise effective (yes/no/partial) with quantified delta
   and recommended next step (e.g. raise further, adjust cheap shape, keep).
4. Reproducible: the analysis script or commands used are referenced so results
   can be re-generated.
data.title: Post-rollout proxy monitoring: warm/cold prefill ratio, fallback rate, remote spend, TTFT

Follow-up implementation for the KV slot save/restore reuse-gap evaluation (parent LP-0MTAQNB7J0094X71, evaluation-only per AC #5). Created by F5 (LP-0MTCMGJBM007AQ55).

Implements the F4/F5 selected fix set for both modes (fast 3 slots cap 83285 / cheap 2 slots cap 126976):

1. CAP RAISE/RESTORE-PATH FIX (dominant, ~22.8M prefill-tokens/day): ensure persistence applies at the routing clamp for oversized sessions (F2 root cause: 38/48 sessions gated out with 0 saves). Raise session_slot_max_prompt_tokens to per-slot clamp (fast 83285, cheap 126976 — pinned per LP-0MTBTCB8D000OQ0C) AND fix the restore path so accepted sessions actually restore (native checkpoint restores at 4.88%). MUST carry the GPU-wedge plan unchanged (LP-0MS91DHPZ001VWQO): timeout base 3.0s + 0.0015s/token, max 60s; cooldown 300s after 3 consecutive failures; skip-when-busy stays on.
2. AFFINITY/SLOT-OWNERSHIP FIX (~3.3M): lease churn (166 orphan + 141 evicted releases/day) breaks session-slot continuity (F2); orphan-cleanup continuity + LP-0MSB0RV72001KNRV registry-leak class.
3. RESTORE-BEFORE-SAVE ORDERING (~0.44M): restore before saving for hot same-slot sessions, zero GPU footprint change.
4. /slots 500 + slots_stale fix feeds affinity: router-mode GET /slots 500s (6,865/day, 100% router-proxied per F3) — direct model-instance polling / last-known-state fallback (F3 fix rank 1).

Reference the F1-F5 deliverables: docs/dev/save-restore-reuse-gap-root-cause.md, docs/dev/slots-500-triage.md, docs/dev/restore-rate-metric-fix-ranking.md, docs/dev/mode-specific-recommendation.md; scripts/slot_persistence_harness.py, slot_reuse_gap_analysis.py, slots_500_triage.py, restore_metric_fix_ranking.py, mode_recommendation.py.

## ACs

1. Fast mode serves oversized sessions (up to the 83285 clamp) with persistence: oversized-session save/restore events appear in the corpus for previously-gated sessions.
2. Cheap mode (cap 126976) likewise persists and restores.
3. Native checkpoint restore rate for >50K contexts improves measurably from the 8.6% baseline (F2), within the GPU-wedge plan (no wedges, cooldown fires as configured).
4. GET /slots router 500s reduce (target router:500 == 0 per F3) and slots_stale drops.
5. Full project test suite passes; no regressions; metrics validated by re-running the F1 harness + F4 metric module.
data.title: Implement KV slot persistence fixes from reuse-gap evaluation (fast cap 83285 / cheap cap 126976)

Implement Lever 1 from LP-0MTED3OLC001RJN4: hold the local pool slot only while the llama-server slot is generating (first-byte onward); release during prefill and immediately after stream end, with a prefill-aware guard to prevent slot exhaustion when concurrent prefills saturate parallel.

## Goal
Reduce false-full `local_concurrency_limit` fallbacks (290/381 = 76.1% of lcl in window 2026-08-28 13:14:52 → 2026-08-29 13:14:52 were during 0 active streams) by counting only generating requests toward `session_slot_pool_size`.

## Context / Evidence
- Investigation LP-0MTED3OLC001RJN4 (T1–T3) + comments:
  - LP-C0MTH6TYQC008RNUD (T1 traceability: data sources + method)
  - LP-C0MTH74FZL005NZ8B (T2 quantified prefill vs busy: 3.46h prefill excluded from 27.9% busy, median 4.14s p90 43.9s max 564.8s; increment→first-byte not derivable without request-ID correlation, bounds given)
  - LP-C0MTH7A92Q008XJ4T (T3 hypothesis CONFIRMED + time-aligned trace + lever table)
  - LP-C0MTH7DYFU004UZOP (T4 recommendation)
- Parent LP-0MTED3OLC001RJN4 ACs + window data (1293 fallbacks, 381 lcl, 290 idle-time)
- Follow-up ranking: Lever 1 > Lever 2 > Lever 3 for remote-spend; Lever 3 > 1 > 2 for local processing time

## Data sources (same as LP-0MTED3OLC001RJN4 T1)
- ~/proxy-usage-reports/2026-08-30/report.md (Generated 2026-08-29 13:14:53, window 2026-08-28 13:14:52 → 2026-08-29 13:14:52, 1293 fallbacks) + fast_sessions.csv, cheap_sessions.csv, errors.csv (44 slot_save errors), errors.json
- /var/log/llama-proxy/llama-server.log-2026-08-28.gz (1537 eval-timing, 7.52h) + llama-server.log-2026-08-29.gz (24, 0.16h); proxy.log.2026-08-28_14.gz (74 lcl burst) with rotation gaps
- proxy/config.yaml (session_slot_pool_size: 3, lease 30s), proxy/config-fast.yaml, proxy/config-cheap.yaml
- proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py:_try_acquire_local_dispatch / _increment/_decrement_local_active_queries, proxy/proxy/provider.py:_get_local_concurrency_info, proxy/proxy/router.py:1092 (Stream started)

## Related work / Invariants
- Must NOT regress contention-queue invariants LP-0MSORQVK50012Q4D / LP-0MSOZF399000NV6I (fast mode 99.2% of lcl; queue is not the contributor — keep LP-0MSORQVK50012Q4D semantics intact)
- Must preserve session_slot_pool_size single source LP-0MTCZ35X7009IZKE
- Leverages LP-0MTAQNB7J0094X71 (KV reuse gap, 95% unrestored) and LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM (ctx-size) for prefill reduction (parallel track)
- Touches lease scope (LP-0MRHV4UYE0013F6P, LP-0MSEHMMBK0062ZPI, LP-0MSU9RL07004FVGO) — narrow to generation-only; adaptive prefill lease (60 + tokens*0.015 cap 1500s + prefill-progress) stays for in-flight prompts
- Orphan-cleanup LP-0MSUO6HLX0089MNQ etc. must remain covered

## Suggested approach
- Change occupancy check in _try_acquire_local_dispatch / _get_local_concurrency_info to count only generating slots toward session_slot_pool_size; release during prefill and on stream end (no inactive 30s hold for non-generating)
- Add prefill-aware guard: check slot_busy / n_past liveness or cap concurrent prefills to parallel before dispatch, to avoid llama-server internal queue saturation
- Add increment→first-byte observability (log measure between dispatch and first chunk in stream_generator) so the next audit can derive the distribution without request-ID correlation

## Acceptance Criteria
- False-full fallbacks reduced: measurable drop in idle-time local_concurrency_limit among the 290 idle events (quantify via next proxy-usage window or benchmark)
- TTFT neutral-to-positive; no regression when parallel=3 is saturated (prefill guard tested)
- session_slot_pool_size remains single source; cheap-mode queue invariants preserved (tests green)
- Tests: unit tests for new occupancy logic + guard; integration harness under proxy/benchmarks/ if added; full suite green
- Docs: update docs/llama-router.md if pool semantics change; CHANGELOG owned by release pipeline

## Notes
- Levers 2 (lease 30s→5–10s post-stream) and 3 (KV reuse/warm-cache) are lower-priority follow-ups; create separate items if/when pursued (see lever table in LP-C0MTH7A92Q008XJ4T)
data.title: Implement generating-only pool with prefill-aware guard to reduce false-full fallbacks
